(a) In General.—Section 1848(e)(1)(E) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395w–4(e)(1)(E)), as amended by section 303 of the Temporary Payroll Tax Cut Continuation Act of 2011 (Public Law 112–78), is amended by striking “before March 1, 2012” and inserting “before January 1, 2013”. 
    (b) Report.—Not later than June 15, 2013, the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission shall submit to the Committees on Ways and Means and Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate a report that assesses whether any adjustment under section 1848 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395w–4) to distinguish the difference in work effort by geographic area is appropriate and, if so, what that level should be and where it should be applied. The report shall also assess the impact of the work geographic adjustment under such section, including the extent to which the floor on such adjustment impacts access to care.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that an "Advisory Commission" is involved, which sounds like an outside advisory body feeding into a federal decision. But the section only extends a statutory date and directs MedPAC, a congressional support agency, to send a study report to congressional committees, which stays inside the federal government. It requires no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission shall submit to the Committees on Ways and Means and Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate a report

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so this is an internal reporting requirement rather than consultation with or participation by parties outside the federal government. The text does not describe any process involving the public, states, or other non-federal entities in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: Not later than June 15, 2013, the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission shall submit to the Committees on Ways and Means and Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate a report
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (MedPAC) is an advisory body that includes outside experts, and thus its work constitutes participation. However, the text does not describe the composition of MedPAC or any process of consulting with outsiders; it merely mandates that MedPAC submit a report to Congress. Since Congress is inside the federal government, this is an internal reporting requirement, not participation by outsiders in a decision.

opus.w: Subsection (a) only changes a date, and subsection (b) only requires MedPAC, a congressional support agency, to report to congressional committees. Reports to Congress stay inside the federal government. The section has no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, or outside consultation before a federal decision. MedPAC's advisory character doesn't make this participation, because its job here is to give Congress an analysis, not to bring outsiders into an agency decision.
opus.s: the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission shall submit to the Committees on Ways and Means and Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate a report that assesses whether any adjustment under section 1848 of the Social Security Act
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes": the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (MedPAC) is an advisory body that includes outside experts, and it is asked for a policy assessment. That reading fails because the only process in the section is a report from MedPAC to House and Senate committees. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted before a federal agency makes a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission to submit a report to Congressional committees. According to the definition, reports to Congress, its committees, or its members are considered inside the federal government and do not constitute participation. There is no requirement for the Commission to consult with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making its decision or report, nor is there any mechanism for outside parties to influence the decision through hearings or comments.
qwen_chat.s: Not later than June 15, 2013, the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission shall submit to the Committees on Ways and Means and Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Finance of the Senate a report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (MedPAC) is an advisory body that includes outside experts, and thus its creation or activity constitutes participation. However, the section itself does not establish the commission or define its membership; it merely mandates that the existing commission submit a report to Congress. Furthermore, the report is directed to Congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are not participation. The section does not require the commission to consult with the public, states, or other outside entities before making its assessment, nor does it grant outside parties a right to sue or comment. Therefore, the interaction is purely internal (agency to Congress).
